security_audit.summary: All 50 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, relative documentation links, metadata URLs, and ordinary planning language. The skill contains no executable shell commands, network requests, dynamic path access, prompt-injection attempt, or data-exfiltration intent. Its instructions explicitly treat imported business data as untrusted and require user confirmation before saving results.

remediation.issue: Static scanners interpret Markdown backticks and relative links as command execution and path traversal.
remediation.suggestion: Use scanner-aware annotations or update detection rules to distinguish Markdown code spans and documentation links from executable commands and file operations.

remediation.issue: The skill may process exports and sponsor materials containing sensitive business data.
remediation.suggestion: Continue to request only necessary aggregate metrics, treat pasted material as untrusted, and obtain explicit confirmation before persisting results.

content.user_title: Plan Newsletter Revenue with Clear Assumptions
content.value_statement: Newsletter revenue planning can mix uncertain conversion, sponsorship, and growth assumptions. This skill builds a labeled model that separates measured inputs from estimates and includes disclosure checks.
actual_capabilities: Builds paid subscription tier models with stated conversion assumptions.
Creates sponsorship rate cards using CPM, CPC, or flat-per-send pricing.
Projects revenue at list-growth milestones using referral or recommendation inputs.
Labels figures as Measured, User-provided, or Estimated.
Flags sponsorship disclosure, claim substantiation, and commercial-consent gaps.
Produces a handoff summary for ROI calculation or quality review.
limitations: It does not fetch ESP, analytics, ecommerce, or ad-network data automatically.
It does not provide benchmark conversion rates, CPMs, prices, or subscriber counts.
It does not calculate ROI, payback, list value, or final quality scores.
It flags legal and consent concerns but does not provide legal advice.

use_cases.title: Price a new paid newsletter
use_cases.description: Model paid tiers and projected subscription revenue from a stated list size, price, and conversion assumption.

use_cases.title: Prepare a sponsor rate card
use_cases.description: Size sellable inventory and compare CPM, click-based, and flat sponsorship pricing.

use_cases.title: Compare growth-led revenue plans
use_cases.description: Project paid and sponsorship revenue at current, 25 percent growth, and 50 percent growth milestones.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple model
prompt_templates.prompt: Model paid subscriptions for my newsletter. I have 8,000 active subscribers, a 38 percent open rate, and a 10 dollar monthly price. Mark every assumption clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Create a sponsor rate card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sponsorship rate card for my 30,000-subscriber newsletter. We send weekly, average 45 percent opens, and have one primary and two secondary placements. Compare CPM and flat pricing.

prompt_templates.title: Compare monetization mixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare paid subscriptions only against a hybrid paid subscription and sponsorship plan. Our list has 45,000 subscribers, 42 percent opens, 3.1 percent clicks, and a 12 dollar monthly tier. Use stated assumptions only.

prompt_templates.title: Plan growth and compliance checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 12-month newsletter monetization plan with referral growth. Show revenue at current size, 25 percent growth, and 50 percent growth. Include disclosure, claim, and consent open loops.

output_examples.input: A 20,000-subscriber weekly newsletter seeks paid tiers and sponsorships.
output: Paid tier: conversion assumption and monthly revenue projection labeled Estimated.
Sponsorship card: primary and secondary placement prices with CPM basis.
Open loops: confirm consent scope and approved sponsor disclosure wording.

output_examples.input: A publisher has no conversion rate or CPM data.
output: The model leaves conversion and sponsorship lines marked [needs source].
It requests the missing data instead of presenting benchmark estimates as facts.

best_practices: Provide active-subscriber counts, engagement metrics, send cadence, and current prices from your own reports.
State each conversion, fill-rate, and growth assumption beside the related revenue line.
Review sponsorship labels, offer claims, and consent scope before selling inventory.
anti_patterns: Do not treat estimated subscription revenue as measured performance.
Do not fill missing CPMs or conversion rates with unsupported industry figures.
Do not include subscribers without commercial-mail consent in sellable audience calculations.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide active subscribers, open and click rates, send cadence, existing revenue, goals, and any price or growth assumptions.

faq.question: Can it create a sponsorship rate card?
faq.answer: Yes. It can model CPM, click-based, or flat-per-send placements and state the inventory and fill-rate assumptions.

faq.question: Will it invent industry benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. Missing conversion rates, CPMs, prices, and growth inputs are marked as needing a source.

faq.question: Does it connect to my email platform?
faq.answer: No. It uses numbers you provide from your own exports. Optional integrations are not required.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROI?
faq.answer: No. It prepares revenue-model inputs and hands return, payback, and list-value math to an ROI calculator.

faq.question: Does it provide legal approval for sponsorships?
faq.answer: No. It flags disclosure, claim, and consent issues for review and does not provide legal advice.
